channel.title: Treasure Coast Today
channel.description: Local news for Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, Florida.

item.title: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
item.description: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club on July 4.

item.title: Juno Beach debates replacing fence at JB-7 beach access as residents report trespassing
item.description: Residents at the Colony Condos say beachgoers are cutting through private property since the town removed a fence at the JB-7 public walkway in 2023. The Juno Beach Town Council will address the fence question during budget discussions on July 15.

item.title: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
item.description: The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher su.

item.title: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
item.description: Riviera Beach is celebrating after being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida community selected for the honor this year.

item.title: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
item.description: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. The district also achieved a record 93.5 percent graduation rate.

item.title: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
item.description: Beth Clark, 48, received a denial from Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before her scheduled breast reconstruction surgery. The insurance company denied coverage for the GalaFlex mesh procedure, calling it investigational.

item.title: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
item.description: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4. The band will represent the entire state of Florida at the prestigious event.

item.title: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4 percent this year, survey finds
item.description: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef is up 5.5 percent and buns are up 7.7 percent.

item.title: Juno Beach condo residents want fence restored at JB-7 beach access after trespassing complaints
item.description: A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, and a fix could cost the town thousands of dollars.

item.title: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
item.description: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance in a deadly home fire earlier this week, with preliminary findings pointing to an electrical issue.

item.description: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.

item.description: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year over social media comments about Charlie Kirk.

item.description: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.

item.description: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.

item.description: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the Fourth of July weekend.

item.title: Hobe Sound woman killed in home fire as community supports grieving fiance
item.description: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a Hobe Sound home fire that preliminary findings suggest was caused by an electrical issue. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.

item.title: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
item.description: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Turnpike as part of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project.

item.title: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof repaired after WPTV intervention
item.description: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien lifted from his home within hours of WPTV contacting the roofing contractor who left two holes unfinished.

item.description: Paula Stark submitted qualifying paperwork less than 30 minutes before the June 12 deadline but failed to include required Form 6, according to state officials who say they cannot verify the document was ever submitted.

item.title: The Woodson African American Museum to reopen with Smithsonian exhibition
item.description: The newly renovated St. Petersburg museum reopens July 11 with an America 250 exhibition, one of only three Florida organizations selected by the Smithsonian for the Many Voices One Nation program.

item.title: Attorney General Uthmeier endorses Byron Donalds in Florida Governor race
item.description: Attorney General James Uthmeier backed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor as multiple Republicans compete to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis.

item.description: The Burg Bid for the Historic Gas Plant District would restore Booker Creek from a drainage ditch to a central natural feature with parks and an integrated Pinellas Trail.

item.description: Secretary of State Cord Byrd said the Universal Primary Contest for House District 47 is already underway with overseas military ballots due July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots mailing July 9-16.
